rationale: This is a cosmetic aggregation variant of the already-tested "Liquidity-Funded Expansion Breadth" (identical three legs, MIN→SUMRANK on the two investment terms only), so it changes the tail-thinning mechanics without introducing any new economic content.

Adding cash depletion to the inventory-up/capacity-down conjunction is a substantive economic discriminator (distress-driven asset shedding vs. benign reallocation) rather than a relabeling, though the triple-MIN will thin the extreme portfolio and the incremental information over the parent signal may be modest.

TREND of invt/che is numerically pathological because cash can be arbitrarily close to zero (1% winsorization will not tame a 3-year trend of an exploding ratio), and the construct largely restates the already-tested "Profitable Working-Capital Squeeze" (high inventory, low cash) in continuous form.

The mechanism — high capex that produces neither net capacity nor retained liquidity — is coherent and the sign logic is internally consistent, but it repeats the same "bolt on NEG(DELTA(che))" move used elsewhere in this batch and builds on a parent whose cross-sectional slope was already weak (fmb −1.10).

Rescaling aqc by che rather than at is essentially a denominator swap on a parent signal that already failed (fmb −0.81), and che is a near-zero-prone scaler that will make the ratio's cross-sectional distribution unstable and winsorization-dependent rather than a cleaner measure of balance-sheet stretch.

The hypothesis (capital deepening that fails to deliver overhead relief signals unproductive investment) is economically clean and the expression matches the stated sign, but both legs have already been tested in adjacent combinations with weak results, so this is a plausible-but-low-prior recombination rather than a new mechanism.
